title: What's Really Inside a Camel's Hump? 🐪
description:
What's inside a camel's hump? Not water: a dromedary's hump stores up to about 35 kg of fat for energy, while its water is spread through its whole body, it can lose about a quarter of its weight in water, and then drink around 100 litres in roughly ten minutes thanks to oval red blood cells that can swell without bursting.

topic: What's really inside a camel's hump?
script: A camel's hump hides up to 35 kilos of fat, not a drop of water. Here's why you never knew. Fat is food in a backpack. When there's nothing to eat, the camel burns that fat for energy, and the hump shrinks and flops over. With all the fat in one lump, the rest of the body stays lean and cool. Okay, so where's the water? It's spread through the whole body. A camel can lose a quarter of its weight in water and keep walking. Its oval blood cells keep sliding along even as its blood thickens. Then it finds a well, and drinks around a hundred litres in about ten minutes. Those blood cells swell to twice their size without bursting. So if you had a hump, what would you store in yours?
key_facts: A dromedary's hump is fat, not water (up to about 35 kg)
Burning the fat for energy makes the hump shrink and flop over
Storing fat in one lump keeps the rest of the body lean, helping heat loss
A camel can lose about a quarter of its body weight in water
Oval red blood cells keep flowing as blood thickens and can swell to about twice their size without bursting
A thirsty camel can drink around 100 litres in about 10 minutes
